vision_features.abnormalities: 1. Exterior bark/outer tissue: The outer surface of the stem is dry, shredded, and peeling away in fibrous strips. Color ranges from tan to dark brown and near-black in places. The texture is dry, papery, and fragmenting. Near the lower portion of the exposed area, there is a discrete, larger dark brown-to-black patch approximately 1–1.5 cm across, irregular in shape, located at the edge of the split section. 4. The outer bark remnants along the edges of the split are tan to light brown with darker brown streaking running lengthwise. No distinct border or halo is observed around individual dark markings within the interior.
vision_features.absences: 1. No powdery or dusty coating is visible on any surface of the stem. 2. No raised pustules, thread-like growths, or fluffy surface structures are visible on the exposed interior. 3. No green or living tissue is visible anywhere on the stem — the entire structure appears fully dried and dead. 4. No visible exudate, slime, or wet/moist areas are apparent on the stem surfaces.
vision_features.summary: The image shows a severely deteriorated, fully dry and dead plant stem in a late-season field setting. The most distinctive feature is the exposed interior of the stem, which displays a prominent, irregular network of thin dark brown-to-black lines forming a closed, maze-like or netted pattern against a pale off-white background tissue. The outer bark is shredded, peeling, and dark brown to black, indicating complete tissue death. A discrete, larger dark patch is also present at the lower edge of the split section. The stem is the most severely affected organ, and the striking dark netted/marbled pattern on the pale interior tissue is the single most unusual visual feature.

Knowledge-base entry for 'Diaporthe':
────────────────────────────────────────
For stem canker, initial symptoms are small, reddish-brown lesions near the nodes in the lower third of the canopy that expand into sunken gray-brown cankers with reddish margins; for pod and stem blight, the most characteristic sign is linear rows of black specks on mature soybean stems.. Mature plants with stem canker can exhibit irregular, thin black lines or 'zone' lines on the interior of lower stems; black specks (pycnidia) appear in linear rows on stems for pod and stem blight.. Knowledge-base entry for 'Phomopsis':
────────────────────────────────────────
Phomopsis-infected seeds are cracked and shriveled and often covered with chalky, white mold. Infected seedlings have reddish-brown, pinpoint lesions on the cotyledons or reddish-brown streaks on the stem near the soil line.. Seeds are cracked and shriveled with chalky white mold covering; seedlings show reddish-brown pinpoint lesions on cotyledons or reddish-brown streaks on stem near soil line.

Knowledge-base entry for 'Phytophthora':
────────────────────────────────────────
Early symptoms include seed rot and damping off; the most characteristic symptom is a dark brown lesion on the lower stem extending up from the taproot, which can girdle the stem causing stunting or death.. A dark brown lesion on the lower stem extending up from the taproot, reaching as high as several nodes, girdling the stem; as disease progresses, damping off, stunting, yellowing, and brown lesions on lower stem can occur.. Small, angular, reddish-brown lesions surrounded by a yellow halo; as disease progresses, lesions often grow together to produce large, irregularly shaped dead areas.. Centers of older lesions frequently fall out, causing leaves to appear tattered; symptoms usually begin in the upper canopy on young leaves.. DISCRIMINATING: 'Diaporthe' vs 'Phomopsis'
Ruling feature : Linear rows of black specks (pycnidia) on mature stems vs. chalky white mold on cracked/shriveled seeds
Diaporthe: Diaporthe produces linear rows of black specks (pycnidia) on mature stems and sunken gray-brown cankers with reddish margins near nodes; interior of lower stems may show irregular thin black 'zone' lines.
Phomopsis: Phomopsis produces cracked, shriveled seeds covered with chalky white mold, and infected seedlings show reddish-brown pinpoint lesions on cotyledons or reddish-brown streaks on the stem near the soil line.
Decision rule  : IF the plant shows linear rows of black specks on mature stems and/or sunken gray-brown cankers with reddish margins, diagnose Diaporthe (Disease A); IF the primary symptom is chalky white mold on cracked/shriveled seeds or reddish-brown pinpoint lesions on seedling cotyledons, diagnose Phomopsis (Disease B).

DISCRIMINATING: 'Diaporthe' vs 'Phytophthora'
Ruling feature : Linear rows of black specks (pycnidia) on stems vs. a continuous dark brown lesion extending upward from the taproot
Diaporthe: Diaporthe (pod and stem blight) produces distinctive linear rows of black specks (pycnidia) on mature stems; stem canker form shows sunken gray-brown cankers with reddish margins near lower-canopy nodes and may show internal black zone lines.
Phytophthora: Phytophthora produces a solid dark brown lesion originating at the taproot and extending upward along the lower stem, potentially girdling the stem and causing stunting, yellowing, or death.
Decision rule  : IF the lower stem shows a continuous dark brown discoloration extending upward from the taproot (no discrete specks), THEN suspect Phytophthora; IF the stem surface displays linear rows of discrete black specks (pycnidia) or sunken cankers with reddish margins at nodes, THEN suspect Diaporthe.
